newsitem.title: UK: British MPs call for tough utility price controls.
newsitem.headline: British MPs call for tough utility price controls.

text.p: An influential committee of parliament on Thursday urged regulators of Britain's water and electricity industries to limit company profits to what was needed for future investment.

The Public Accounts Committee said in a report that in the first five years after privatisation water companies made 7.4 billion pounds ($11.8 billion) in profits and regional electricity companies 8.7 billion.

Both these figures were higher than the regulators have judged reasonable for the future, said the report, published just ahead of an election in which the opposition Labour Party will promise a windfall tax on some utility company profits.
The committee said it was important "to avoid the risk that profits might again rise above a reasonable level".

"We recommend that the Directors General (regulators) set price controls which will ensure that profits should be no more than sufficient to provide the return required to attract the necessary funds for investment in future periods," it said.

The committee said although the profits allowed for by regulators of privatised ultilities had varied in the past between four and 15 percent of capital, there was now an increasing consensus around 6.5 to 7.5 percent.
"We are concerned, however, at the time that it has taken for such a consensus to develop," it said.

The report also looked at the regulation of Britain's privatised gas and telecommunications companies -- firms which like the water and electricity firms have been widely criticised for paying their directors huge salaries and perks.
It said regulators had told the committee they could not get involved in remuneration issues.

But it added: "We recommend...that the directors general impress on companies the risks they face, in terms of loss of public confidence and trust, if they pass excessive emoluments to top executives, and that they seek ways of influencing companies to avoid unjustified levels of pay." ($1=.6281 Pound)
